about: Identity-aware proxy deployment guide (US-SPEC-18 section 8). Data, read by core/doors/proxy.js: each step names the check that observes it done, so the guide cannot drift from the code. A step a person must do outside the console becomes a decision card that closes when its check passes (US-18-R09). The console's own sign-in stays on as the inner lock.

steps.what: Add the console address as a self-hosted application in your Zero Trust dashboard, covering /console and /api/console
steps.default_in_effect: the console stays behind its own sign-in only

steps.what: Add an Allow policy that lists the people who may open the console, and copy the application audience tag into the settings
steps.default_in_effect: nobody is let in by the proxy; the console's own sign-in still works

steps.what: A request with no proxy sign-in is turned away before it reaches the console
steps.default_in_effect: the console's own sign-in is the only lock

steps.what: The console's own sign-in is still required behind the proxy
steps.default_in_effect: the proxy would be the only lock

steps.what: Put the service behind an HTTPS load balancer and switch Identity-Aware Proxy on for its backend service
steps.default_in_effect: the console stays behind its own sign-in only

steps.what: Set the service to accept traffic from the load balancer only, so the proxy cannot be bypassed
steps.default_in_effect: the service address stays reachable directly; the console's own sign-in still guards it

steps.what: The console's own sign-in is still required behind the proxy
steps.default_in_effect: the proxy would be the only lock
